prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit / identity-preserve. Edit target is Image 1, the approved-direction Mina dragon with a small stylized body and huge dark wings. Image 2 is the original Mina, reference ONLY for the wing ornament motifs: white frilled trim, dark navy ribbon, blue jewel. Make exactly TWO changes: enrich the wings with Mina-specific ornament and lengthen the tail. Do not redesign the character.
LOCK ALL OTHER FEATURES: Keep exactly the same delicate face, blue eye shape and quiet expression, black swept fringe, head size, small compact stylized bipedal torso, two independent little arms and two bent hind legs, current wing-to-body size ratio, airborne pose, left-facing three-quarter view, linework and soft anime shading. The user likes this balance. Do not enlarge or lengthen the torso, make it muscular or adult-human proportioned, shrink the face, change to four-legged anatomy, change the wing silhouette to butterfly wings, or add body armor. Wings remain the visual main feature.
CHANGE 1, MINA MOTIFS ON WINGS ONLY:
- Keep the enormous wing membranes predominantly BLACK and deep navy. Preserve the broad clean dark areas. Do not fill them with white.
- Along the existing thin ivory scalloped trailing edge, add a restrained second finer scalloped seam and tiny fan-fold divisions that recall Mina's white maid frills. This is integrated wing patterning, not an actual garment draped over the wings. The border should look refined and recognizable at game-sprite size, not busy all-over lace.
- Near each wing's structural root/upper knuckle, add a small dark NAVY ribbon-knot-shaped ornamental marking set around a clear small BLUE diamond jewel, echoing Mina's collar ribbon and chest brooch. These are compact design accents, much smaller than the face, and must not obscure wing anatomy or turn into giant bows.
- Extend a few fine blue/ivory curved lines along existing wing supports, naturally joining these small jewel motifs to the scalloped edge. Let the pattern feel like the quiet order of Mina's apron folds, but do not add random flowers, gold armor, stars, or other characters' symbols.
- Decoration increases through structure and small detail, NOT large white areas. White remains a narrow accent, roughly no more than 5-8 percent of the overall character. No new aura or floating particles.
CHANGE 2, LONGER TAIL:
Lengthen the existing tail by roughly 40 percent while keeping its original thickness at the base and an elegant taper. Let it flow backward to the right and then curve downward in a long fluid S, following the force of the wingbeat. Preserve the current black/navy tail design, small ivory edge and restrained blue accents. Not a thick muscular tail, not a second torso, not split tails or ribbons; one continuous anatomically connected tail. Keep it behind/below the small body without crossing the face, hands, or wing ornaments. Do not shrink the whole character to fit the tail; expand the transparent canvas/margins as needed.
Single complete character. All wing tips and the new tail tip fully within frame with comfortable margin. Preserve actual alpha transparency, no background, no checkerboard pixels, no gradients or glow outside the silhouette, no scenery, no ground shadow, no text or watermark. The only new artwork belongs to the wing ornaments and lengthened tail; the approved small body and face must be kept.
